title: Crosswave burst probe — arrival entrainment scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory probe of a two-frequency (crosswave) arrival pattern to see if the batcher/kv-cache interplay creates periodic tail amplification. This is a personal scratchpad — rough notes, results, and immediate hypotheses.

Hypothesis:
- Mixing two near-harmonic arrival frequencies (f1 ~ 3Hz, f2 ~ 3.6Hz) causes transient alignment epochs where requests cluster and produce >x tail amplification at p99 compared to steady Poisson of same avg qps.
- KV cache hit-rate oscillates with same beat frequency, magnifying latency when cache miss windows align across tenants.

Setup (quick):
- Cluster: 4x A100-80GB, CUDA 12, runtime @ commit abc1234 (batcher + evictor tweaks).
- Model: rw-13b-8k-qat-int8 (serving variant: int8, fused attention).
- Runtime config: max_batch_tokens=16384, max_batch_size=64, batch_timeout_ms=15, preemptive_prioritization=on, early_flush=off.
- Traffic generator: custom harness (go), sends timestamped arrivals with arrival time = t + sin(2pi f1 t)*A1 + sin(2pi f2 t)*A2, peak amplitude A1=0.25s, A2=0.18s; envelope scaled to reach instantaneous peaks up to 1.8x base QPS.
- Base target QPS: 250 (sustained average), duration: 30m runs.
- Metrics exported: qps (1s), concurrency, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (ms), cpu/gpu util, kv_cache_hit_rate (per shard), batch_size distribution, dropped/rescheduled counts.

Run notes (session A — 2024-11-08 10:00 UTC):
- seed: rng-20241108-01
- f1=3.0 Hz, f2=3.6 Hz, base qps 250, amplitude scaling -> transient spikes to ~450 qps for ~3-7s when waves align.
- Observed outer behavior: GPU util hovered 72-88% during peaks, baseline 55-60%. Batcher average batch size increased from 18 -> 42 during alignment.

Summary table (aggregated windows):
| window | avg qps | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | kv_hit% | dropped% | notes |
|--------|--------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|-------|
| baseline (off-peak) | 240 | 28 | 64 | 95 | 82.1 | 0.0 | steady batches ~18 |
| alignment peak | 430 | 45 | 132 | 310 | 57.3 | 0.4 | many large batches, queuing + kvcache misses |
| recovery | 260 | 32 | 78 | 120 | 78.9 | 0.05 | batcher flush and cache warming |

Instantaneous p99 spike pattern (ASCII timeline — 60s slice, p99 in ms):
[0s]  85  92  110  135  180  245  310  290  230  150  120  95  80  76  88  102  140  220  290  305  210  160  110  90  82  

Batch size distribution note:
- median 18, 90th 38, max observed 64 (matches max_batch_size). Large batches correlate strongly (rho ~ 0.73) with p99 in the alignment windows.

Logging snapshot (important lines):
- [10:23:14] batcher: formed batch size=62 tokens=10240 latency_queue_ms=12
- [10:23:16] runtime: kvcache miss shard=3 keyset=transient miss_rate=0.68
- [10:23:17] preempt: preempted 3 low-priority requests, rescheduled -> added 18ms extra wait

Immediate observations / working hypotheses:
1) Aligned crosswave peaks produce short-lived demand bursts that exceed the warmup capacity of the kvcache and cause larger, cold batches. Cold batches have heavier memory/KV misses and longer service time per token.
2) Batcher parameters (batch_timeout_ms=15) allow large growth in batch size during a burst; early_flush would have limited max batch size at cost of throughput. There's a tradeoff between throughput efficiency and tail protection.
3) Preemptive priorities mitigated some tail but caused jitter in p50/p95 for low-priority lanes — need per-tenant QoS profiling.

Comparisons vs Poisson control (same avg qps):
- Poisson run produced p99 ~ 110ms vs crosswave p99 median ~ 210ms (approx +90ms). kv_cache hit-rate was ~81% for Poisson vs ~62% for crosswave.

Quick experiment matrix to run (next):
- E1: Reduce batch_timeout_ms to 8ms, keep other params, repeat crosswave. Measure p99 delta and throughput loss.
- E2: Enable early_flush=true (threshold 40%) to limit large batches, repeat.
- E3: Increase KV cache shard size by 25% (simulated) to see if hit-rate improves during alignments.
- E4: Add randomized jitter to arrival timestamps (uniform +/- 50ms) to decorrelate alignment; test whether that smooths tails (if yes, consider inferred smoothing in front proxy).

Preliminary E1 quick run (2024-11-09 14:15):
- batch_timeout_ms=8ms -> p99 reduced from peak 310ms -> 180ms (approx -130ms), but throughput during peak dropped ~7%, GPU util peaking 78% -> 70%. kv_cache hit-rate improved slightly during alignment (61% -> 64%). Dropped/rescheduled increased marginally 0.4% -> 0.6%.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Is this user-visible? For typical request payloads (avg tokens ~ 220), p99 bursts to 300ms are noticeable. But if majority of traffic is interactive (strict SLOs), we should prefer tail protection.
- Can we implement adaptive batch_timeout based on short-window qps slope? Might tighten timeout as slope increases.
- Where does the preemptive scheduler hurt fairness? Capture per-tenant latencies next run.
- Check correlation between shard-level kvcache eviction cycles and external orchestration events (spot reclaim?). Look at node-level logs around alignment time.

Quick actionables (one-liners):
- Run E2 + per-tenant traces (assign to Ravi).
- Add short-term dashboard: beat-frequency p99 overlay + kvcache hit-rate (chart).
- Draft RFC: adaptive batch timeout heuristic (outline skeleton in /confluence/perf/adaptive-batcher).

Appendix: quick commands used
- traffic harness: ./crosswave-gen --f1 3.0 --f2 3.6 --amp1 0.25 --amp2 0.18 --qps 250 --dur 1800 --seed rng-20241108-01
- metrics export: prometheus -> csv (downsample 1s)
- analysis notebook: local/notebooks/crosswave-20241108.ipynb (plots + correlation matrices)

End of scratchpad — want to keep this short and iterate. Will paste cleaned results in perf channel after E2/E3 runs.
